steps.title: (i) Find the conjugate of iu

lines.text: The conjugate changes the sign of the imaginary part.

steps.ask: On the diagram, which side of the imaginary axis is $-b + ai$ on, and where is its reflection?
steps.title: (ii) Plot iu and its conjugate

lines.text: $iu = -b + ai$ is the point $(-b, a)$: left of the imaginary axis and a small height above the real axis.
$\hl{1}{\overline{iu}} = \hl{1}{-b - ai}$ is the point $(-b, -a)$, the reflection of $iu$ in the real axis.

steps.ask: What does multiplying by $i$ do to a point, and what does the conjugate do after that?
steps.title: (iii) Describe a transformation from u to the conjugate of iu

lines.text: Multiplying by $\hl{2}{i}$ turns $u$ into $iu$: a rotation of $\hl{2}{90^\circ}$ anticlockwise about the origin.
Then reflecting $iu$ in the real axis gives $\hl{1}{\overline{iu}}$.

problems.final: iu = -b + ai,\ \hl{1}{\overline{iu} = -b - ai};\ \text{rotate } \hl{2}{90^\circ} \text{ anticlockwise about the origin, then reflect in the real axis}
